touches.text: Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

Deleting code is about running code, not about the record of what happened. A retired path that something still CALLS is the defect; a retired path named by a record of what passed through (history, state, validations, verdicts, a measured fixture) is not. Requirements that police history are de-emphasized, because the aim is less history noise in front of Claude, not hidden history (Law 5). Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#99 (ticket c8e421aac06e's measured fixture names skills/ruled/intention+why.json and the retirement tooth read it as a caller): "we are trying to remove as much of the history as we can. not hiding it, but reducing the noise you're exposed to. time to de-emphasize requirements like that."

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf. The gates are CodeMother's (9.3.5).
